data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 identifies 'configural items' as the single-evaluation discriminator but fails to provide the causal mechanism linking configural item performance to genuine reliability. The target never establishes why succeeding on configural items demonstrates that the panel is using a genuine causal reasoning process rather than having memorized a checklist rule that happens to be more complex. A sophisticated checklist can explicitly encode instructions for configural interactions (as SRC_002 even admits in its counterconditions). Because the target lacks a causal mechanism distinguishing deep 'configural processing' from mere 'compliance with a configural rule,' its proposed evidence cannot distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance on those items.
